steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Watercolour relies on the white of the paper for luminosity — work from light to dark, preserving highlights. | Key Fact: Acrylic is versatile: thin it for washes or apply thickly (impasto) for texture; it dries quickly so you can layer rapidly. | Key Fact: Wash techniques include flat wash (even tone), graded wash (light to dark), and wet-on-wet (blended, soft edges). | Key Fact: Glazing (thin transparent layers over dried paint) builds depth and richness in both watercolour and acrylic.
